idiom_name: Express + Passport: req.user filled by deserializeUser, guarded by req.isAuthenticated()
implementation_notes: Node's standard library has no identity type; the dominant realization is Passport as Express middleware: a strategy verifies the credential, serializeUser stores only an identifier in the session, deserializeUser loads the descriptor and Passport attaches it to the request as req.user, with req.isAuthenticated()/req.login()/req.logout() completing the contract. The classic authenticator/descriptor/factory structure collapses into one initialize/passport.session() pair plus per-strategy callbacks, and the session carries an id rather than the attributes, so attribute changes take effect on the next request. For stateless bearer tokens, hand-roll a tiny middleware that sets req.subject - consumers still just ask the request who is acting.
pitfalls: req.user only exists after passport.session() has run: routes or middleware registered before it see no user, and reading req.user.id without isAuthenticated() throws for anonymous requests.
A fat req.user serialized into the session both bloats the session store and freezes attributes; deserialize a minimal descriptor per request instead.
req.user is per-request mutable state: handlers that enrich it change the identity every later middleware sees - keep the descriptor read-only.
